chains.title: Alt G creates a GC-box that gains KLF5/SP-family binding at a CCDC50-region enhancer
chains.element: Putative intronic/intergenic enhancer at chr3:191.44 Mb within or near CCDC50

links.claim: The T>G substitution raises local GC content and can complete a GC-box/CACCC-like element, so the alt allele is bound more strongly by KLF/SP-family zinc fingers; within this specificity group KLF5 is chosen because it is the KLF most highly expressed in colonic epithelium and colorectal cancer lines such as HCT 116.
The variant lies in a candidate cis-regulatory element (open chromatin / H3K27ac-marked enhancer) active in colonic epithelium, not in a protein-coding exon.
That element loops to and regulates CCDC50, the nearest expressed gene at the locus.
KLF5 is abundant in proliferating intestinal crypt epithelium and in HCT 116, so the allelic difference is realised in that cell type.
Increased KLF5-driven expression of the target gene supports crypt progenitor proliferation and modestly increases colorectal cancer risk.

predictions: Alt allele shows higher reporter activity in HCT 116 and higher KLF5 ChIP/CUT&RUN signal
KLF5 knockdown collapses the allelic reporter difference
Effect is epithelial-specific, absent in lymphoblastoid cells
falsified_if: No KLF/SP footprint or ChIP signal over the variant in colon epithelial cells
QBiC/SELEX shows no KLF-family score gain for alt G
Reporter shows ref > alt or no difference

chains.title: Ref T preserves a TCF7L2 Wnt-response element; alt G disrupts it

links.claim: The TCF/LEF consensus (CTTTG(T/A)(T/A)) is T-rich, so a T>G change at such a position lowers predicted affinity; TCF7L2 is chosen from the TCF/LEF specificity group because it is the dominant family member in colonic epithelium and HCT 116.
The variant sits in an enhancer carrying clustered TCF/LEF motifs typical of colorectal Wnt-response elements.
The enhancer contacts CCDC50 (or, alternatively, the more distal FGF12) and sets its basal expression.
Constitutive Wnt/beta-catenin signalling in colonic adenoma and carcinoma cells makes TCF7L2 occupancy functionally consequential there.
Altered Wnt target dosage shifts crypt stem-cell dynamics and changes colorectal cancer risk.

predictions: TCF7L2 ChIP-seq peak over the variant in HCT 116 with allelic imbalance favouring T
Reporter activity drops with alt allele and is beta-catenin dependent
Effect lost upon TCF7L2 knockdown or Wnt inhibition
falsified_if: No TCF7L2 ChIP signal at the locus in colorectal lines
No TCF/LEF motif match on either strand around the variant
Reporter difference unaffected by Wnt pathway manipulation

chains.title: Ref T supports a CDX2 homeodomain site controlling an intestinal enhancer

links.claim: CDX/caudal-type homeodomain sites are A/T-rich (TTTAT core), so alt G is predicted to reduce binding; within the CDX specificity group CDX2 is chosen because it is the intestine-restricted member expressed in colon and HCT 116, whereas CDX1 is lower and CDX4 absent.
The variant lies within an A/T-rich intestinal enhancer bound by CDX2/HNF4A-type lineage factors.
The element acts over a longer range on FGF12 rather than the nearest gene.
CDX2 is an intestinal master regulator, limiting the effect to colonic epithelium.
Weakened CDX2-dependent enhancer activity blunts differentiation programmes and slightly raises colorectal cancer risk.

predictions: Allelic effect present in colon lines but not in non-intestinal cells

falsified_if: No CDX2 binding at the variant
